translation_en: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, ‘Amr al-Naqid, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, and Ibn Abi ‘Umar narrated to us—and the wording is ‘Amr’s. Ishaq said: Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah informed us; the others said: Sufyan narrated to us, from ‘Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Yazid, who heard Ibn ‘Abbas say: Usamah ibn Zayd informed me that the Prophet said: “Usury is only in deferred exchange.”

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: ‘Affan narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me: Bahz narrated to us. They said: Wuhaib narrated to us: Ibn Tawus narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn ‘Abbas, from Usamah ibn Zayd, that the Messenger of Allah said: “There is no usury in what is exchanged hand to hand.”

Al-Hakam ibn Musa narrated to us: Hiql narrated to us, from al-Awza‘i, who said: ‘Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah narrated to me that Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri met Ibn ‘Abbas and asked him, “What do you think of your view on currency exchange? Is it something you heard from the Messenger of Allah or found in Allah’s Book, Mighty and Sublime?” Ibn ‘Abbas said, “No. Regarding the Messenger of Allah, you know better than I; and regarding Allah’s Book, I do not know it there. But Usamah ibn Zayd told me that the Messenger of Allah said: ‘Indeed, usury is only in deferred exchange.’”

‘Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us—and the wording is ‘Uthman’s. Ishaq said: He informed us; ‘Uthman said: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, who said: Shibak asked Ibrahim, who narrated to us from ‘Alqamah, from ‘Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah cursed the one who consumes usury and the one who pays it. I asked, “And its recorder and two witnesses?” He said, “We only report what we heard.”

Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah, Zuhayr ibn Harb, and ‘Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Hushaym informed us: Abu al-Zubayr informed us, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah cursed the one who consumes usury, the one who pays it, its recorder, and its two witnesses, and said: “They are all alike.”

Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Numayr al-Hamdani narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Zakariyya narrated to us, from al-Sha‘bi, from al-Nu‘man ibn Bashir, who said: I heard him say—I heard the Messenger of Allah say, as al-Nu‘man pointed to his ears with his fingers: “The lawful is clear and the unlawful is clear, and between them are doubtful matters that many people do not know. Whoever avoids doubtful matters safeguards his religion and honor; whoever falls into doubtful matters falls into the unlawful, like a shepherd grazing near a protected pasture who is likely to graze in it. Every king has a protected pasture, and Allah’s protected pasture is what He has forbidden. There is a piece of flesh in the body: if it is sound, the whole body is sound; if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt. It is the heart.”
Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Waki‘ narrated to us; Ishaq ibn Ibrahim informed us: ‘Isa ibn Yunus informed us. Both reported from Zakariyya with this chain and a report like it.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim informed us: Jarir informed us, from Mutarrif and Abu Farwah al-Hamdani; Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id narrated to us: Ya‘qub, Ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman al-Qari, narrated to us, from Ibn ‘Ajlan, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa‘id. All reported from al-Sha‘bi, from al-Nu‘man ibn Bashir, from the Prophet, with this hadith, though Zakariyya’s report is more complete and detailed.

‘Abd al-Malik ibn Shu‘ayb ibn al-Layth ibn Sa‘d narrated to me: my father narrated to me, from my grandfather: Khalid ibn Yazid narrated to me: Sa‘id ibn Abi Hilal narrated to me, from ‘Awn ibn ‘Abd Allah, from ‘Amir al-Sha‘bi, who heard al-Nu‘man ibn Bashir ibn Sa‘d, a Companion of the Messenger of Allah, address the people in Hims. He said he heard the Messenger of Allah say: “The lawful is clear and the unlawful is clear,” then mentioned a report like Zakariyya’s from al-Sha‘bi up to “is likely to fall into it.”

Abu al-Tahir Ahmad ibn ‘Amr ibn Sarh informed us: Ibn Wahb informed us, from Malik ibn Anas, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ‘Ata’ ibn Yasar, from Abu Rafi‘, that the Messenger of Allah borrowed a young camel from a man. When camels from the charity levy arrived, he told Abu Rafi‘ to repay the man with a young camel. Abu Rafi‘ returned and said, “I found only a fine, mature camel.” He said: “Give it to him, for the best people are those best in repaying.”

Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Khalid ibn Makhlad narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ja‘far, who said: I heard Zayd ibn Aslam: ‘Ata’ ibn Yasar informed us, from Abu Rafi‘, the client of the Messenger of Allah, who said: The Messenger borrowed a young camel, with a report like it, except that he said: “The best servants of Allah are those best in repaying.”

Muhammad ibn Bashshar ibn ‘Uthman al-‘Abdi narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja‘far narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: A man was owed something by the Messenger of Allah and spoke harshly to him. The Prophet’s Companions were about to deal with him, but the Prophet said: “The one who is owed has the right to speak.” He then said to them, “Buy him a camel of the same age and give it to him.” They said, “We can find only one older and better than his.” He said: “Buy it and give it to him, for the best among you—or the best of you—are those best in repaying.”

Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Waki‘ narrated to us, from ‘Ali ibn Salih, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah borrowed a camel and repaid with one older than it, saying: “The best of you are those best in repaying.”

Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Numayr narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: A man came demanding a camel owed to him by the Messenger of Allah. He said: “Give him a camel older than his.” He added: “The best of you are those best in repaying.”

Yahya ibn Yahya al-Tamimi and Ibn Rumh informed us: al-Layth informed us; Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id narrated it to me: Layth narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: A slave came and pledged allegiance to the Prophet for emigration, unaware that he was a slave. His master came seeking him. The Prophet said, “Sell him to me.” He bought him for two black slaves. After that, he would not pledge allegiance to anyone until asking, “Is he a slave?”

Yahya ibn Yahya, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, and Muhammad ibn al-‘Ala’ narrated to us—and the wording is Yahya’s. Yahya said: Abu Mu‘awiyah informed us; the other two said: Abu Mu‘awiyah narrated to us, from al-A‘mash, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad, from ‘Aishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah bought food from a Jew on credit and gave him an iron coat of mail as collateral.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali and ‘Ali ibn Khashram informed us: ‘Isa ibn Yunus informed us, from al-A‘mash, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad, from ‘Aishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah bought food from a Jew and pledged an iron coat of mail as collateral.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali informed us: al-Makhzumi narrated to us: ‘Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad narrated to us, from al-A‘mash, who said: We mentioned pledging collateral in advance sales before Ibrahim al-Nakha‘i. He said: Al-Aswad ibn Yazid narrated to us, from ‘Aishah, that the Messenger of Allah bought food from a Jew on credit and pledged an iron coat of mail of his as collateral.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated this to us: Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, from al-A‘mash, from Ibrahim, who said: Al-Aswad narrated to me, from ‘Aishah, from the Prophet, a report like it, but he did not mention that it was iron.

Yahya ibn Yahya and ‘Amr al-Naqid narrated to us—and the wording is Yahya’s. ‘Amr said: Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah narrated to us; Yahya said: Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah informed us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Kathir, from Abu al-Minhal, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said: When the Prophet came to Madinah, people were making advance payments for fruit one or two years ahead. He said: “Whoever pays in advance for dates should do so for a known measure, a known weight, and a known term.”

Shayban ibn Farrukh narrated to us: ‘Abd al-Warith narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih: ‘Abd Allah ibn Kathir narrated to me, from Abu al-Minhal, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah came while people were making advance payments. He said to them: “Whoever pays in advance must do so only for a known measure and a known weight.”

Yahya ibn Yahya, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, and Isma‘il ibn Salim all reported from Ibn ‘Uyaynah, from Ibn Abi Najih, with this chain and a report like ‘Abd al-Warith’s, but without the phrase “for a known term.”

Abu Kurayb and Ibn Abi ‘Umar narrated to us: Waki‘ narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us: ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us. Both reported from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, with their chains and a report like Ibn ‘Uyaynah’s, including “for a known term.”

‘Abd Allah ibn Maslamah ibn Qa‘nab narrated to us: Sulayman, Ibn Bilal, narrated to us, from Yahya, Ibn Sa‘id, who said: Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab used to report that Ma‘mar said the Messenger of Allah said: “Whoever hoards is in error.” Sa‘id was asked, “But you hoard.” He said: “The Ma‘mar who used to narrate this hadith also used to hoard.”

Sa‘id ibn ‘Amr al-Ash‘athi narrated to us: Hatim ibn Isma‘il narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn ‘Ajlan, from Muhammad ibn ‘Amr ibn ‘Ata’, from Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab, from Ma‘mar ibn ‘Abd Allah, from the Messenger of Allah, who said: “No one hoards except one in error.”

Ibrahim said: Muslim said: One of our companions narrated to me, from ‘Amr ibn ‘Awn: Khalid ibn ‘Abd Allah informed us, from ‘Amr ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn ‘Amr, from Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab, from Ma‘mar ibn Abi Ma‘mar, one of Banu ‘Adi ibn Ka‘b, who said the Messenger of Allah said a report like Sulayman ibn Bilal’s from Yahya.

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: Abu Safwan al-Umawi narrated to us; Abu al-Tahir and Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us. Both reported from Yunus, from Ibn Shihab, from Ibn al-Musayyab, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah say: “An oath helps sell goods but erases profit.”

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Kurayb, and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us—and the wording is Ibn Abi Shaybah’s. Ishaq said: He informed us; the other two said: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from al-Walid ibn Kathir, from Ma‘bad ibn Ka‘b ibn Malik, from Abu Qatadah al-Ansari, who heard the Messenger of Allah say: “Beware of frequent oaths in sales, for they promote the sale and then erase its blessing.”

Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us: Zuhayr narrated to us: Abu al-Zubayr narrated to us, from Jabir; and Yahya ibn Yahya informed us: Abu Khaythamah informed us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said the Messenger of Allah said: “Whoever has a partner in a house or date palm must not sell it until he informs his partner. If the partner agrees, he may take it; if he dislikes it, he may leave it.”

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Numayr, and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us—and the wording is Ibn Numayr’s. Ishaq said: He informed us; the others said: ‘Abd Allah ibn Idris narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ruled that pre-emption applies to every undivided jointly owned property, whether a house or garden. A partner may not sell until informing the other partner; if the other wishes, he may take it, and if he wishes, he may leave it. If it is sold without informing him, he has the greater right to it.
